pattern.crimePattern: informal lender loses his temper over a small debt
pattern.notes: Fictional lender and vendor; Jeevanjee Gardens is a public setting only.

ob.reportedBy: Bakari Mwamba, county gardener, Jeevanjee Gardens
ob.text: County gardener Bakari Mwamba reports that newspaper and airtime vendor Patrick Njoroge (47) was found collapsed under his kiosk awning at Jeevanjee Gardens at 15:25, after the afternoon downpour. Pronounced dead at the scene.

people.name: Patrick Njoroge
people.occupation: Newspaper and airtime vendor, Jeevanjee Gardens
people.bio: Sold newspapers and airtime from the same kiosk for fifteen years. Kept his accounts in a school exercise book.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 40s, round glasses, a sleeveless sweater over a shirt, a bundle of folded newspapers under one arm, warm crinkled smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Bernard Langat
people.occupation: Runs 'Langat Credit', a small lending business
people.bio: Lends small sums to traders around the CBD at high interest. Patrick owed him KSh 10,000.

image.brief: Kenyan man, around 50, long grey raincoat, trilby hat, a leather collection book in his hand, hard patient expression, ID-photo framing

people.name: Tony Kariuki
people.bio: Helps at the kiosk and collects the afternoon papers. Quarrelled with his uncle about wages last week.

image.brief: Kenyan young man, early 20s, oversized football jersey, a bundle of afternoon newspapers tied with string, red eyes from crying, ID-photo framing

people.name: Fredrick Ouko
people.bio: Sells newspapers at the other gate of the gardens. Has applied to the county for Patrick's better pitch.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 30s, neat shirt and tie, a plastic folder of county forms, defensive and offended, ID-photo framing

people.name: Esther Muthoni
people.bio: Buys airtime from Patrick every weekday on her way home to Kangemi.

people.name: Bakari Mwamba
people.bio: Tends the flowerbeds at Jeevanjee. Found Patrick.

people.name: Wilfred Kamau
people.bio: Hands out the Taifa Jioni bundles. Speaks to Amani by phone.

locations.name: Jeevanjee Gardens
locations.description: A small public park in the CBD, crowded at lunch, empty in rain. The downpour began at 14:50 and stopped at about 15:30. Everything is soaked: the benches, the grass, the paths. Patrick's kiosk stands under a small tin awning by the north gate.

hotspots.label: Under the kiosk awning
hotspots.text: Patrick lies half under the awning, half out of it. The report says one blow. Amani crouches: the ground under his body is dry. Everything around it is soaked.

hotspots.label: Beside the kiosk
hotspots.text: A closed black umbrella leans against the kiosk. It isn't wet inside its folds. A sticker is on the handle.

hotspots.label: Kiosk drawer
hotspots.text: Airtime cards, a cash tin with a few hundred shillings, and a school exercise book of accounts.

hotspots.label: Toilet block
hotspots.text: Bakari Mwamba and two other gardeners shelter here when it rains.

body.text:
Thursday:
Airtime — Mama Esther 100 (14:35)
Langat 10,000 — paid 2,000 today. Balance 8,000.
Tony's wages — talk Saturday.

facts.text: Patrick Njoroge was found under his kiosk awning at 15:25, after the downpour.
Patrick was struck once, hard, on the side of the head.
The ground under Patrick's body is dry, though everything around it is soaked. He was lying there before the rain began.
The umbrella's handle sticker: 'Langat Credit — Mikopo Haraka', with a phone number.
The umbrella is dry inside its folds: it was left closed before the rain and never opened.
Patrick's book, today: 'Langat 10,000 — paid 2,000 today. Balance 8,000.'
Patrick's book, today: 'Airtime — Mama Esther 100 (14:35).'
Bakari: the rain began at ten to three and stopped at about half past.
Bakari sheltered in the toilet block with two other gardeners from 14:50 until 15:25, then found Patrick.
Bakari: Patrick's nephew Tony goes to the newspaper depot every afternoon for the Taifa Jioni.
Bakari: Fredrick Ouko, who sells papers at the other gate, wants Patrick's pitch.
Esther bought airtime from Patrick at 14:35. He was fine.
A man in a long grey coat with a black umbrella was waiting beside the kiosk 'like a man waiting to be paid.'
Esther left on the 14:38 matatu to Kangemi and shows the fare receipt.
Esther: "Langat? The lender? Yes, that was him in the grey coat at the kiosk, twenty-five to three."
Dispatcher: Tony collected the Taifa Jioni bundle at 14:30 and waited for the second van until 15:05.
Fredrick's Huduma Centre ticket C-114: issued 13:58, served 15:21. He was inside the whole time.
Bernard: "I collect from forty people a week. I don't remember every one."
Bernard: "I lend money. I don't break heads. Dead men don't pay."
Bernard says he 'lost an umbrella somewhere this week.'
Tony and his uncle argued about wages last week; they were meant to talk on Saturday.
Fredrick has applied to the county for Patrick's pitch. He was at Huduma Centre about it today.

interrogations.intro: Bakari is still holding his rake. "Fifteen years he sold me the Taifa every morning. Fifteen years."

topics.reply: He owed some people money. Everyone does. He was a good man with bad luck.
Tony goes for the Taifa Jioni every afternoon. Industrial Area. He wasn't even here.

interrogations.intro: Esther comes back to the gardens when she hears, still in her church scarf. "I saw him at twenty-five to three. He gave me my airtime and a joke."

topics.reply: Langat? The lender in the grey coat? Yes, that was him waiting at the kiosk, twenty-five to three. I know that coat; he collects at my church too.
A black umbrella, closed, hooked over his arm. It wasn't raining yet.

interrogations.intro: Bernard answers the number on the sticker on the second ring. He comes to the gardens in the same grey coat, carrying a new umbrella.

topics.reply: I give those umbrellas to customers. Advertising. I lost one somewhere this week.
Two thousand, yes, he paid two thousand. On a ten-thousand loan. I told him I'd come back next week.

interrogations.intro: Tony arrives with the afternoon papers and drops them in a puddle. "Uncle?"

topics.reply: We argued about money. He said Saturday. Now there's no Saturday.

interrogations.intro: Fredrick takes a ticket out of his wallet before Amani asks for anything. "I know what people will say. Here."

topics.reply: I wanted his pitch. Through the county, with forms. Not like this.

prosecutor.pass: Dry ground, a dry umbrella and a man waiting to be paid. That will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. When did he fall? The ground is telling you.
No. Narrow the time first. Then ask who was standing at that kiosk in it.

proof.concludes: Patrick was attacked after 14:35 and before the rain began at 14:50.
In that window the man waiting at the kiosk was Bernard Langat, there to collect a debt, and he left his own umbrella behind.

eliminations.why: Tony was at the newspaper depot from 14:30 to 15:05.
Fredrick was inside Huduma Centre from 13:58 to 15:21.
Esther left on the 14:38 matatu, with Patrick alive behind her.
Bakari sheltered in the toilet block with two other gardeners from 14:50 until he found Patrick.

reconstruction.text: Patrick owes Bernard Langat KSh 10,000. On Thursday he has two thousand.
14:35. Esther buys her airtime. A man in a grey coat waits beside the kiosk with a closed black umbrella over his arm.
Patrick pays two thousand and asks for time. Bernard loses his temper and strikes him once.
14:50. The first heavy drops fall. Bernard runs for the bus, leaving his umbrella against the kiosk. The rain soaks everything except the ground under Patrick.

tier1.line: It rained for forty minutes. Look at the ground under him, and ask yourself when he fell.

tier2.line: Alive at 14:35, on the ground before 14:50. Now ask the customer who was standing there.

glossary.def: Service. Huduma Centres are government one-stop service offices.
Respectful way to address an older woman.
